why: The Rust CDR decode cursor, and the anchor for `CdrReader::*`. rclrs has no serialization surface at all -- `Subscription` hands a typed message straight out of `rcl_take`, and the decode is inside the middleware. In ROS 2 the CDR encoder belongs to the MIDDLEWARE, not the client library: `rosidl` generates a `rosidl_message_type_support_t` whose function table is filled in by whichever rmw implementation is loaded (FastCDR inside rmw_fastrtps, the ddsi stream writers inside rmw_cyclonedds), and the only byte-level verbs rcl/rclcpp expose are `rmw_serialize`/`rmw_deserialize` on a whole message. No cursor, no per-primitive call, nothing to correlate against. nano-ros has no middleware plugin to hide an encoder inside -- `nros generate-c` emits the `_serialize`/`_deserialize` body into the USER's translation unit and that TU links against libnano_ros -- so the primitives have to be exported symbols. The RTOS constraint that earns it is the one `c:message_type_t` already records: one linked backend, no runtime typesupport registry to dispatch through. The RTOS scenario is the same one the C side names: a generated `Deserialize` impl compiled into a `no_std` image, decoding from a borrowed `&[u8]` receive buffer into `heapless` storage with no allocator. Note where this is actually consumed. Generated Rust message crates spell `nros_core::{CdrReader, CdrWriter, Serialize, Deserialize, SerError, DeserError}` (packs/nros/message.rs.jinja:7-8), the generated C++ FFI shim crates spell `nros_serdes::` (examples/px4/cpp/bridge/ffi/src/lib.rs:19), and the `nros::` re-export the parity report sees (nros/src/lib.rs:208) is a THIRD publication of the same six items whose only in-tree consumers are two QEMU test/bench bins (nros-tests/bins/cdr-roundtrip-qemu, nros-bench/wcet-cycles-qemu). No example uses the facade spelling. Kept where it is by phase-506 W1 (RFC-0071 D12): it already sits behind `nros::internals` / `nros::embedded` or is a C seam, outside the top-level Rust user API D12 is about.
